description: For twenty years, the United States committed an immense force to Vietnam to curb communism. They get bogged down, divide, and leave without having won.

hero.hook: The leading world power facing a war that it cannot win.

blocks.text: At the heart of the Cold War, Vietnam was split in two. In the North, a communist regime. In the South, a state supported by the West. The United States is sending enormous resources there. Yet they get bogged down.
This conflict is not only military. It divides America, shows the limits of brute force, and leaves lasting trauma on both sides.

After the French defeat in the **[[Indochina War]]**, the Geneva Accords (**1954**) partitioned Vietnam at the **17th parallel**. In the North leads, nationalist and communist leader. In the South, an authoritarian regime supported by Washington. **[[Ho Chi Minh]]**

American presidents **John F. Kennedy** then **Lyndon B. Johnson** fear the **[[The domino theory]]**: if one country falls to communism, the neighbors would follow. In **August 1964**, a naval incident in the Gulf of Tonkin serves as a pretext to expand the war. From **1965**, operation bombs the North, and the Marines land in Da Nang. **[[Rolling Thunder]]**

sections.title: A divided country, then a growing war

blocks.text: In **1969**, approximately **543, 000** American soldiers were on site. The **[[search and destroy]]** strategy (seek the enemy to destroy it) and air superiority did not disrupt North Vietnamese supplies via the Ho Chi Minh Trail. General **Vo Nguyen Giap**, military leader of the North, is banking on the harassment and support of part of the population.

The Americans also use defoliants like Agent Orange to clear the jungle. The human and political cost is exploding. The coffins come in. , US Defense Headquarters, discovers that local political will can hold up in the face of technology. **[[Pentagon]]**
More than **80 million** liters of herbicides were released, destroying approximately **20%** of South Vietnam's forests.

**January 30, 1968**, during the Vietnamese New Year,  hits more than **100** cities. On the ground, it is a failure for the North. On American television, it was a shock: the “near victory” announced by Washington seemed false. **[[Tet Offensive (January 1968)]]**

President **Richard Nixon** then launched “Vietnamization”: withdrawing American troops while arming the South. The Paris Accords (**1973**) marked the American departure. Without a protector, Saigon, the capital of the South, collapsed in two years.

sections.title: The shock of the Tet offensive

blocks.text: **April 30, 1975**, Saigon falls. About **58, 000** Americans died. Vietnamese losses numbered in the millions. The first truly televised war, the conflict also revealed crimes like the **[[My Lai]]** massacre, where American soldiers killed civilians in **1968**. America emerges more suspicious of distant interventions.

blocks.text: After **20 years** of conflict, the United States left Vietnam without victory: military power politically defeated, country reunified under communism, American society lastingly divided.
